countingRules: One entry is one distinct GLB deliverable (ADR-030 item 1). Two files with the same geometry are one entry.
A finish (brass, walnut) is a runtime material, never a file (ADR-030 item 2).
A piece that repeats is one file placed several times as instances (ADR-030 item 3).
A machine is its part files plus its housing files; no assembled-machine file duplicates part geometry (ADR-030 item 5).
Decorative and structural rows of a machine board are nodes of one housing file unless a blueprint makes them player-placed slots (ADR-030 item 4; see machineSlotPlans).
An entry with placeholder true or status BLOCKED records a spec-fixed need whose identity is undecided. It carries a blockedBy reason and no invented geometry.
Future-world entries are not made until the owner approves a world (directive, multiple-worlds requirement sections 8 and 9; ADR-028 rule 4).

integrationStatus INTEGRATED means the real runtime loads a file for the entry. For the two M0 entries (status REWORK_REQUIRED) that file is the legacy file named in legacy; the file at glbPath does not exist until it is regenerated. tools/asset-status.mjs counts them as legacy M0 files, not under Integrated, which counts status INTEGRATED only.

An entry the owner removes is deleted from assets[] and recorded in meta.removedByOwnerDecision with its former classification and status, so the audited count stays traceable. Removed entries are not counted (ADR-039).

Every entry has exactly one scopeClass of the four in meta.scopeClasses (directive, world-by-world strategy, 'Production discipline': shared, world-specific, reused and future planned). It is derived from classification, worldId and reuseEligible, so a change to any of those changes scopeClass in the same edit; tools/asset-status.mjs reports a disagreement and prints the count per class. The four counts add up to the total, each counts unique deliverables only, and a finish or a colour is never a member of any class (ADR-030).
meta.budgetBasis: ADR-034 category ceilings. Allowances per asset are set at Stage 1 so that the scene totals of ADR-034 hold.
meta.dimensionsConvention: approxDimensionsM is [x width, y height, z depth] in glTF axes (Y up), metres; null for an unspecified axis. A rotating part has its rotation axis on local Z (ADR-020), so its thin axis is z. dimensionsBasis says where the number comes from: spec, measured, derived, board (appearance only, ADR-029), unspecified (Stage 1 proposes, the lead approves).

scopeClasses.name: shared
scopeClasses.rule: A competition entry (G0-required or G0-optional) with worldId shared: world-neutral design, such as the mechanical component library, that every world uses without a copy.

scopeClasses.name: world-specific
scopeClasses.rule: A competition entry with a world's identity (worldId is a world, today tockton) and reuseEligible false: it belongs to that world only.

scopeClasses.name: reused
scopeClasses.rule: A competition entry with a world's identity (worldId is a world) and reuseEligible true: made under one world, usable unchanged by another. It is one entry under its own world and is never copied into another world's inventory (for example workbench).

scopeClasses.name: future-planned
scopeClasses.rule: An entry whose classification is not G0-required or G0-optional (G1 to Research): planned, not made before delivery (ADR-028). It wins over the other three, so a future entry is never counted as competition scope.

notes: Only 4 of 12 slots are named in writing: main spring, cylinder, comb, governor (PRODUCT_SPEC section 6.1).
The 12-row Music Box boards (Exploded, Assembly) omit the governor that the spec requires; the governor is one of the 12 (ruling I-6).
Whether the winding key and the case count inside the 12 is open (G-02). The mapping above counts both, which leaves 2 slots without any support.
Drive gear and pinion tooth counts are undecided (G-11); they use library spur gears.
The 20-row board (Carousel 20-Part) matches the spec count and the 0.5 rad/s speed; the 9-row board (Carousel Hero) does not and is not used for the part list.

The board drives the Carousel from the Music Box; SIMULATION_SPEC section 10.2 says its stored energy decreases over time. No spring or key row exists on the board, so the energy source is open: it may add 1 or 2 slots beyond 20.
Board canopy stripes are red; the palette has no red.

The 24-row board (Windmill 24-Part) has no millstone, but the spec requires one and its speed is the Windmill target (windmill_millstone is entered from the spec). 24 board rows plus the millstone make 25, so one board row must be dropped or merged: the lead decides (candidates: the decorative shutters, window frames, door).
Ambient wind drives the sails (ruling I-7). Whether the player also winds the Windmill is open (G-01).
The Bakery has no part count and sits outside this plan.

The 32-row board (Clock Tower 32-Part) matches the spec count but has no clock hands, which the spec requires (real local time). clock_hands is entered from the spec; 32 board rows plus the hands make 33, so one row must be dropped or merged (lead).
Machine targets are undefined and must not be invented (G-13). The Clock Tower is G0-optional and cut first.
